newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases, market still bullish.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases, market still bullish.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange index eased on Friday as investors kept a wary eye on the market but an underlying bullish tone remained, dealers and brokers said.
"Overall compared to last week, the index continued upward on heavy trading on selective shares by foreign investors," a bourse official said.
But on Friday, the index lost 7.13 points to 3492.24 while turnover was at 32.444 million shillings on 619,123 shares from 36.039 million shillings on 696,477 shares on Thursday.
On Friday last week, the 20-share index closed at 3466.92 while turnover was posted at 9.633 million shillings on 188,533 shares, stock exchange figures showed.
Foreign investors bought 125,600 shares of Sasini Tea & Coffee at a reserve price of 73 from 60, Kenya Commercial Bank at 93 from 90, and Firestone East Africa at between 30 and 33 from 30.25.
Power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting gained a further 2.0 shillings to close at 127. Brokers said there were over 10,000 bids for the share at 132, meaning the share stood to make further advances.
"The market is generally bullish right now, although in a toned-down manner," a senior broker said.
Barclays Bank closed at 118 from 116 while Standard Chartered traded at 56.50 from 55.50. Kenya Airways was firm at 9 from 8.90.
The plantations accounted for 15 percent of total volume and registered marginal gains. Rea Vipingo closed at 12.60 from 11.50 while Brooke Bond was unchanged at 150.
The East African corporate bond traded 11 million shillings at 99.99 percent.
